Lapis 1.0.0 is the first stable version. Projects made with 0.10.0 open as they are.

## New

- **Prefabs** — drag an entity into the Assets panel to save it as a `.lprefab`, then place it as often as you like.
  Copies are blue in the Hierarchy and stay locked until unpacked; **Open Prefab** changes every copy at once, and
  scripts place copies with `Instantiate(prefab, position)`.
- **Animation** — skeletons and animations from glTF models exported from Blender. The **Animator** picks the start
  animation, previews every animation in the Scene view and blends smoothly between them with `Play("Run")`.
- **Navigation** — bake a navigation mesh in the new **Navigation** tab (agent radius, height, step height and the
  steepest slope agents climb). Creatures with a **Nav Mesh Agent** find their way around walls, through doors and
  up stairs and ramps, and step out of each other's way. Uses DotRecast.
- **In-game UI** — **Create > UI** adds a canvas with panels, images, text (any `.ttf` / `.otf` font) and buttons
  that call a script method. Elements are moved and resized in the Scene view and anchored for any resolution.
- **Sound** — `.wav` and `.ogg` sounds, **Audio Source** (2D or 3D, loop, pitch, play on start) and **Audio
  Listener**, through OpenAL Soft.
- **Character Controller** — moves players and creatures without passing through walls: stairs, slopes, jumping,
  pushing loose objects. The scripting guide has a ready first-person player.
- **Lights** — spot lights, and spot and point lights now cast shadows too.
- **Fog and fades** — exponential or linear fog in Scene Settings, and `Screen.FadeTo` for fading the picture to a
  colour.
- **Colliders** — capsule and cylinder shapes; the Collider tool (key 4) resizes colliders by dragging dots in the
  Scene view.
- **Community** — **Join the Community** in the project launcher opens the Lapis Discord server.

## Improved

- The renderer uses only OpenGL 4.1 features (the picture is unchanged).
- New guides: the editor, prefabs, animation, navigation, UI and the architecture of the engine; the README is a
  short introduction with links to them.
- Large parts of the engine and editor were reorganised so they are easier to work on; behaviour is unchanged.
- The test process no longer crashes at exit (the sound device is now closed properly).

## Downloads

`Lapis-Windows-x64.zip` and `Lapis-Linux-x64.tar.gz`. They include .NET, so nothing else needs to be installed.
Installed editors offer the update in the project launcher.
